report_name: Microsoft Patches 974 Flaws, Two Exploited Zero-Days in Record Update

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: Actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880 are being used by threat actors to gain SYSTEM-level permissions on compromised Windows systems.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-81963
vulnerabilities.description: An actively exploited elevation-of-privilege vulnerability in the Windows Update Stack, which a locally authenticated attacker can leverage to execute code with SYSTEM privileges due to an improper link resolution.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-85880
vulnerabilities.description: An actively exploited elevation-of-privilege vulnerability in the Windows Advanced Local Procedure Call (ALPC) system. This heap-based buffer overflow allows an attacker to escape an AppContainer sandbox and elevate privileges to SYSTEM.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-69730
vulnerabilities.description: A 'wormable' use-after-free Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in the Windows DNS Server. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit it to execute code on a domain controller.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-69829
vulnerabilities.description: A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in Windows Shell which could allow for arbitrary code execution.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-69595
vulnerabilities.description: A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in Windows Services for NFS which could allow for arbitrary code execution.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-78510
vulnerabilities.description: A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in Microsoft Word which could allow for arbitrary code execution.

indicators.name: Suspicious Child Process from Browser or Office Application
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Child Process from Browser or Office Application
id: 2a9b8c7d-1e3f-4a5b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects command-line interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) being spawned by common browser or Microsoft Office applications. This can be an indicator of post-exploitation activity, such as privilege escalation following a successful phishing attack or browser exploit, as seen with CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880.
references:
  - https://shattered.io/microsoft-patch-tuesday-974-bugs-2-zero-days-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-10
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
      - '\WINWORD.EXE'
      - '\EXCEL.EXE'
      - '\POWERPNT.EXE'
      - '\OUTLOOK.EXE'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects command-line interpreters spawning from browsers or Office applications, a potential sign of privilege escalation.

indicators.name: Anomalous DNS Server Queries
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous DNS Server Queries
id: 3b8c7d2a-f1e3-4b5a-9d8c-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: Monitors for malformed or unusually long DNS queries that could indicate exploitation attempts against vulnerabilities like CVE-2026-69730 in Windows DNS Server.
references:
  - https://shattered.io/microsoft-patch-tuesday-974-bugs-2-zero-days-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-10
tags:
  - attack.t1210
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|re: '.{255,}'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects unusually long DNS queries which may be an attempt to exploit CVE-2026-69730.
